newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bank shrs soar on fund buying, steady rates.
newsitem.headline: Canada bank shrs soar on fund buying, steady rates.

text.p: Shares in Canada's big banks soared to new heights on Tuesday, buoyed by a steady interest rate outlook and the influx of cash into tax-sheltered retirement savings plans.
The banks and trusts index gained 86 points in heavy midday trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange, while the broader financial services group was up 65 points.
"The main driver is the flow of funds into mutual funds. This is the savings season and that buying power is coming into stocks," said Mark Maxwell, a banking analyst with CIBC Wood Gundy.
Bank of Montreal was the top gainer, jumping 1.10 to 48.80 on 484,000 shares after earlier hitting a 52-week high of 49.10.
Bank of Nova Scotia added 1.05 to 49.65 on volume of 244,000 shares. Scotiabank reached a 52-week peak of 49.75 earlier in the session.
Royal Bank of Canada, the country's biggest bank, rose 0.45 to 51.10 on 624,000 shares after a 52-week high of 51.25.
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce gained 0.80 to 62.15 on 768,000 shares. CIBC earlier hit a new high of 62.50.
Toronto-Dominion Bank rose 0.50 to 38.05 on 721,000 shares after a 52-week peak of 38.15. National Bank of Canada edged up 0.20 to 14.65 on 816,000 shares after reaching a high of 14.75.

A steady interest rate environment had also been favorable for the banks, analysts said. The Bank of Canada said on Tuesday that it expected the Canadian economy to grow in 1997 while inflation remained low.
Another positive factor was the group's strong earnings outlook. The banks were on track for record earnings in 1997, but the growth rate would be down year-over-year, Maxwell said.
